## TL;DR

Human task completion now uses the existing teleported confirmation dialog with a six-row report textarea. Reports are submitted with the done transition and retain multiline markdown through task-file serialization and parsing. The screenshot fixture now opens a human task drawer without requesting a diff from a synthetic branch. The required scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

The task branch already contained the core modal and its integration in `TaskDrawer.vue`: selecting Mark done opens `HumanTaskDoneDialog`, and confirming calls the same `setStatus("done", report)` path used to transition a human task from the status control. The modal is composed from the shared dialog primitives, lives in a body Teleport, and uses the shared `cc-modal`, `field`, and button styles. Its shared dialog content supplies the overlay layer marker and the standard overlay dismissal, close, and Escape behavior. The submit handler supports Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, and the textarea receives focus when the modal opens.

I completed the textarea sizing by setting six visible rows explicitly. This makes the intended multi-line report space clear in the rendered form and works with the existing responsive dialog width and resize behavior. The optional label and copy already describe that an empty report is accepted. The status update passes an empty string as a status-only write; the writer ignores whitespace-only notes, so the completion still succeeds without introducing a blank activity note.

The existing note writer records text as a single activity event and converts subsequent lines to blockquote continuation lines. That representation keeps the activity entry attached to its timestamp and survives the task body’s Markdown normalization. I strengthened the note test with a completion report containing a blank paragraph, markdown list items, and a verification limitation. The test transitions the task to done and checks the post-write parsed result, verifying both the status and report content remain present after serialization and reload parsing.

The queued handoff failure reported that the screenshot route was stuck on “Loading full diff…” using the `card:noChanges` fixture. That fixture intentionally creates a fake branch to exercise the no-changes card state. Opening a drawer on the Changes tab therefore caused the app to request a diff for a branch that is not present in the preview environment. I updated the shot declaration to use the `card:humanStep` fixture and a normal Work drawer route, and made that fixture human-assigned so its Mark done action is available. The fixture has no fake branch, removing the source of the pending diff request while retaining the human-task context required for the screenshot.

## Approaches tried

I first ran the focused dialog and task-note tests. The dialog test mounts the real Vue component with its Teleport active, types a multiline report into the rendered textarea, then clicks Cancel and Mark done using actual DOM button clicks. The first note-test run exposed an incorrect expectation in my test: the writer correctly prefixes every continuation line, including blank lines and markdown list items, with `> `. I updated the expected serialized representation rather than changing the writer’s established activity format. The rerun passed all six focused tests.

For the screenshot failure, I traced the specified fixture through the preview fixture switch. `card:noChanges` seeds a branch and zero diff stats, while the shot’s `/work?...&tab=changes` route causes the drawer to load a full diff. The replacement uses the existing needs-human-step fixture, gives that fixture a human assignee, and opens the drawer at its default tab. This preserves the scenario while avoiding an unnecessary branch diff request.

## Challenges and blockers

The required validation took substantial time because RepoOS first waited for a remote runner slot, then its local rendered contrast and UI smoke steps waited for the shared Playwright slot. The remote gate completed successfully; local contrast and smoke also completed successfully once the slot was available. No code or test failure remained.

The first test run failed only because the test expected the second markdown list item without its serialized list marker. Inspection of the actual parsed activity body showed the writer had preserved the text and formatting; I corrected the assertion and reran the affected tests successfully.

## Key learnings

For task-file activity, a multiline note is persisted as one timestamped entry followed by blockquote continuation lines. Blank lines are represented as `> ` and markdown list lines as `> - ...`; tests should assert against that serialized form while checking that task parsing preserves the content. For drawer screenshots, the fixture should avoid inventing a branch unless the screenshot actually exercises branch-backed diff behavior. A normal task drawer can be captured from the default drawer tab without invoking the full-diff loading path.

The completed checks included remote build and typecheck, the scoped changed-path test run, rendered contrast, UI smoke, and local format, lint, CSS layering, theme contrast, hardcoded-color, and bare-require guards. Each completed check passed.
